findings.title: Kept follow-up findings are written to disk unredacted
findings.detail: `keep(_:file:for:)` writes `text` straight to a file under `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` with no redaction. Everywhere else in this file that hands review text to an agent (e.g. `handOff`/`quote`, which calls `vault.forAgent` before writing) redacts before touching disk; here the quoted blocking findings (which can literally be the reviewer quoting a secret it flagged, e.g. a hardcoded key) sit in plaintext under `/tmp` (or the platform temp dir) for the whole life of the follow-up review job, relying entirely on a later, separate step (`Attachments.copy`'s `leaks.redact`) to clean it before the agent ever reads it. A reviewer or anything else with access to that temp folder sees the raw secret in the meantime, and `forget` only removes it once the whole review job ends, not once it's been copied into the worktree.

findings.title: Attachment is created even when `followUp` can never use it
findings.detail: `reviewPublished` keeps and attaches the quoted-findings file whenever `previous.verdict == .changesRequested`, without checking `previous.branch != nil`. `Review.followUp`, which actually consumes that attachment, additionally requires `previous.branch != nil` and falls back to a full review (ignoring the file) when it's missing. For any `Review` record without a stored branch (e.g. one persisted before this field existed, or one that otherwise never got a branch recorded), Oby still writes `review-N.md` into the new review job's `.oby/inputs` and spends the `keep` I/O, but the prompt never mentions or uses it, leaving a stray, unexplained file in the agent's inputs.

findings.title: Follow-up items accumulate without de-duplication
findings.detail: `followUps = (author.review?.followUps ?? []) + (findings?.later ?? [])` simply concatenates every round's "worth doing later" items. Since a follow-up reviewer is told to check the new commits and isn't instructed to avoid repeating a still-unaddressed earlier non-blocking note, the same finding text can be appended again, so `Review.report` (and the pull request comment) can end up listing duplicate follow-ups across rounds.
